title: At-Tin: the fig and the olive
hookLine: by the fig, the olive, Sinai and the safe city, the human was made in the best stature (Surah 95)

lines: BY THE FIG AND THE OLIVE.
cards: A companion of the Prophet named al-Bara' remembered one night on a journey. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ led the evening prayer and recited a short surah that starts with fruit: by the fig and the olive.
Al-Bara' said, and it's recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari, that he had never heard anyone with a more beautiful voice or recitation.
Of all the things he might have remembered from his time with the Prophet, he remembered a voice, at night, reciting about figs.

teach.h: FIG, OLIVE, SINAI, THE SAFE LAND.
teach.b: Surah ninety-five opens with four oaths, in Pickthall's translation: By the fig and the olive, By Mount Sinai, And by this land made safe. Why fig and olive? Commentators give two answers, and hold both.
The fruits themselves, gifts of the earth, sweet and nourishing. And the places they grow: some commentators link the fig and olive to the lands around Jerusalem, home to earlier prophets.

Mount Sinai is where Musa received revelation, and this land made safe is Mecca, where the Prophet was. So some scholars read the oaths as a map of revelation: the lands of the prophets, Musa's mountain, Muhammad's city.
Then the point of all four oaths: Surely We created man of the best stature.
Ahsan taqwim: the finest form, the best proportion, body and mind and soul. That's the Qur'an's starting point about human beings: made well, beautifully, on purpose.

teach.h: THE LOWEST OF THE LOW, EXCEPT —
teach.b: Then a hard line: then We reduced him to the lowest of the low. Commentators read it several ways: old age and frailty, or the fall that comes when a person turns away. Except, it says, those who believe and do good.
They have a reward that never ends.
So the surah holds both: made in the best form, and able to fall far from it. The dignity is the beginning, not something you have to earn. What you do with it is the story.

how: At-Tin is recited in the prayers, and the Prophet recited it in the evening prayer while traveling; its verse on the best stature is often quoted in teaching about human dignity.

o: the clay the first human was shaped from
the olive oil that lit the lamps of old
the fig, the first oath of Surah ninety-five

games.q: what's inside the oaths — tap the pairs.
p: the best stature, the finest form

s: the surah says humans are made badly and must fix themselves
it says man was created of the best stature (95:4).
al-Bara' remembered the Prophet reciting it at night on a journey
and said he never heard a more beautiful voice (Bukhari).
commentators agree the fig and olive are only fruit
some read them as fruit and also as the lands where they grow.

games.q: the surah says man was made in the best stature, then reduced to the lowest of the low. who is the exception?
o: those who believe and do good
games.why: those who believe and do good have a reward that never ends (95:6). the dignity is the start; what you do with it is the story.

practice: Hold a fig or an olive, or any fruit, and look at it closely, the color, the skin, how it's put together; then eat it slowly, and if you pray, say bismillah first and alhamdulillah after.
If you don't have one, look at your own hand the same way: the joints, the lines, how it moves.

wordCard.voice: At-Tin. The fig, the first oath of Surah ninety-five, which says the human was made in the best stature. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the fig; the first oath and the name of Surah 95.

carryVoice: Your line: made in the best form. That goes for the face in the mirror, and for every other face too. Until tomorrow.
